Tiie Lords Commissioners for regulating, directing, approving, and confirming all Sales, and Contrails for Sale, made by Bodies Politic or Corporate, or Companies, and by all Feoffees and Trustees for charitable or other public Purposes, and by all Persons holding under any Grant from the Crown, or under any Ait of Parliament, any Estates wherein His Majesty, His Heirs or Successors, have any Interest or Expedancy ;—having received His Majesty s directions to lay before this House,

A Statement of their Proceedings since the 24th of June 1803, distinguishing the number and value of the Sales, and Contrails for Sale, approved by the said Commissioners; the Amount of Land Tax redeemed, or to be redeemed by virtue of such Sales and Contrails for Sale; the quantity of Stock purchased by the produce of such Sales; the Gain to the Public resulting from the Proceedings under the said Commission; the Expence incurred; and the estimated Value of the entire Property of which the Tenure has been, or will be changed, by the effect of such Sales, or Contrails for Sale; —

In adjusting and approving the terms and conditions of Sale, it has been anxiously and invariably the object of the Lords Commissioners to establish and maintain certain uniform principles calculated to prevent any improvident Sales, and beneficial as well as safe to the property of the Church, and of other Corporate Bodies, as far as might be compatible with the nature of the Property to be disposed and with the different tenures to which that Property might be subject.

Pursuing these principles, the Board have found it necessary to difeufs many questions of intricacy and detail with respect both to legal conftradions and to modes of valuation.

Their minutes and decisions have been consequently very volumi* nous, and have been accurately and carefully entered and preserved.

The Lords Commissioners take this occasion again to acknowledge the ready and efficient affiffance and attention which they have experienced from time to time, from His Majesty’s Law Officers, from the Directors of the Bank, the Commissioners for the Reduction of the National Debt, and from the Officers of the Bank of England.

The current business of the Commissioners, as will appear in the two following Sedions of this Report, is gradually diminishing; Hill; however, it is considerable and important.

A STATEM ENT of the Proceedings of the Lords Commissioners for regulating, directing, approving, and confirming all Sales, and Contracts for Sale, made by Bodies Politic or Corporate, or Companies, for the purpose of Redeeming their Land Tax; from the 29th of March 1799 to the 24th of June 1803.

To the Honourable the Commons of the United Kingdom of Great Britain and Ireland, in Parliament assembled. u The Lords Commissioners for regulating, directing, approving, u and confirming all Sales, and Contracts for Sale, made by * Bodies Politic or Corporate, or Companies, for the purpose of u Redeeming their Land Tax," have received His Majesty’s Directions to lay before the House of Commons—A Statement of their Proceedings, distinguishing the Number and Value of the Sales, and Contracts for Sale, approved by the said Commissioners; the Amount of Land Tax redeemed, or to be redeemed, by virtue oi such Sales, and Contracts for Sale; the Quantity of Stock purchased by the Produce of such Sales; the Gain to the Public resulting from the Proceedings under the said Commission; the Expence incurred, and the estimated Value of the entire Property of winch the Tenure has been, or will be changed, by the efted of such Sales, or Contracts for Sale; — And the said Commissioners Report accordingly:

I.—By an Act passed the 21ft March 1799, " to amend and render " more effectual the preceding Acts for the Red* mption and Purchase •* of the Land Tax," it was made lawful for Ills Majesty to appoint feveti Persons of His Majestys most Honourable Pi ivy Council, to be Commissioners for regulating, directing, approving, and confirming all Sales, and Contracts for Sale, made by Bodies Politic or Corporate, or Companies, for the purposes of redeeming any Land Tax charged on any of the Manors, Meflfejges, Lands, Tenements, or Hereditaments, belonging to such Bodies Politic or Corporate, or Companies.

And His Mace fly, by Letters Patent under the Great Seal of ’Great Britain, bearing date the 26th March 1709, nominated and appointed the Right Honourable William Lord Auckland, the Right Honourable Henry Addington' (then Speaker of the House of Commons) the Right Honourable William Pitt, the Right Honourable the Master of the Rolls (now Lord Alvanley) the Right Honourable Sir William Wynne, Knight, the Right Honourable the Lord Chief Baron, and the Right Honourable Syivefler Douglas (now Lord Glenbervic) for the purposes of the said recited Act, and with authority to any two or more of the said CommissionevS, to do any ad, matter, or thing, which by the said Commission the said Commissioners are authorized to do: And various Legislative Provisions have since been made, to facilitate and extend tha ©peratioa-and-fcffed of the said Commission.

Their Meetings have been continued from time to time by adjournments, of more or less frequency, according to the nature and importance of the business to be transaded; and the ttoftumflioners have acted with the advice of

V.—The Amount of Land Tax redeemed, or to be redeemed, by virtue of such Sales, and Contracts of Sale, cannot yet be stated with precision, as in several instances the Money arising from Sales approved and confirmed by the Lords Commissioners has not yet been paid into the Bank. Besides which, the Property sold by the Corporate Bodies, being required by Law to be sold free and discharged from Land Tax, ^ther Land Tax has, in very many cases, by Agreement between the Parties, been freed by the Lessee or Purchaser at his expence.

It is therefore difficult to ascertain what Amount of Land Tax may have been redeemed by this part of the operation.

On the whole, however, the Ariiount of Land Tax redeemed, or to be redeemed, by virtue of the aforesaid Sales, and Contracts for Sale, may be estimated at about £.40,000. per annum.

VI. —The quantity of Stock purchased by the Bank from the produce of such Sales, is, £. 1,12*000.; exclusive of the sums not paid into the Bank, and also of Sums not yet brought to account, amounting together, by Estimate, to £. 284*000. Stock.

VII. —The Gain resulting to the Public from the Proceedings under the Commission^ consists rtioft immediately in the 1/1 ith required by the Acts to be paid to the Publit beyond the value-of the band'Tax^ TCfieemed, and such Gain cannot be stated at less than £. 140,006. Stock; and this is exclusive of the Land Tax redeemed by the Lessees and Purchasers of many considerable Parcels of the Property sold to them. -A further Gain resulting to the Public from the Proceedings under the Commission, is to be found in the general operation of the Redemption of the Land Tax, particularly by creating a daily demand of a certain proportion of Stock, which can never be brought back into the Market.

The efled of that circumstance is evidently beneficial; and Public Credit has been materially affified, by thus withdrawing from the Market upwards of Twenty Millions of Stock, in little more than Four Years, for the Redemption of Land Tax.

There are nlfo other descriptions of Gain to the Public, which are not inconsiderable, when collectively taken, by the accumulation of the 1-1 ith beyond the amount of the Land Tax fold; by the saving of the Allowances to the Receivers General; by the Stamps on Renewal of Leases, and on Conveyances of settled Leasehold Estates.

And, in a more direct point of view, the Sales made by the Proceedings under the Commission may he considered as beneficial to the Public, by giving local accommodations to the Purchasers, by multiplying the means of Improvement, and by increasing the Revenues of the Corporate Bodies, in some infiances very considerably.

VIII.—The Expence incurred has been refirided within the nar-rowefi limits to the Salaries of a Chief Secretary, Affifiants, and CJerks; the Fees of Counsel, the Rent of the Office, and certain small incidents; the whole amounting on the average of Four Years to about £.1,550. per annum.

IX.—The value of the entire Property, of which the Tenure has been changed by the effect of the Sales, and Contracts for Sale, has been computed to be not less than three times the Amount of the whole Sum received. Afliiming this computation to be well founded, the Amount fold or contracted for being £. 852,063. the value in Fee of the whole Property transferred from Corporate Bodies will be

The Prices approved in Sales, and Contracts for Sale, have varied from Six to Nine Years Purchase, for the Reversion in Fee of Lands and Tythes under Leases, for Three Lives; from Eight to Fourteen Years Purchase, for the Reversion in Fee of Lease for Twenty-one Years: —Five Years Purchase has been taken for Houses let for

Thirty Years > and Three Years for the Reversion in Fee of Lades for Forty Years. Reserved Rents and Property, not let on beneficial Leases, have been fold for Twenty-five to Thirty Years Purchase.

X. —'There cannot be a doubt that tkefe Sales are convenient to Purchasers, advantageous to the Sellers, find their Successors, and highly beneficial to the Public in general; and therefore the Lords Commissioners would gladly have added to this Report, some Estimate of the Proportion of Land Tax puyable, and hot yet redeemed by the Bodies Corporate.

It is however difficult to arrive at any certainty in this part of the Enquiry. It is probable that the- Proportion of Land Tax redeemed by Corporate Bodies, and their Lessees, may exceed the Proportion as yet redeemed by other descriptions of Property, chargeable with Land Tax; ftiH however it may he estimated, that nearly Two* thirds remain unredeemed.

XI. —The general Results may be dated to be»

That the number of Sales approved is, 1,778.

That the Amount in Money of such Sales, so approved, i» £. 852,063 fierling.

That the value in Fee Simple of the Property fold, is abovt £. 2,500,000. fierling.

That the Stock purchased for the Redemption of Land Tax* under the Proceedings of the Commissioners, is about £.1,300,000.

That the whole Expence to the Public has been £. 6,950.

That the Gain to the Public, by the operation, has not been less than £. 140,000 Stock, exclusive of the other benefits explained and detailed in this Report.

By Order of the Lords Commissioners,

Young,

King’s Warrant; -granting Additiona Salary of 1,500 per annum to the Right honble Hemy I Lord Viscount f Melville, as Keeper of the Privy Seal of Scotland. -

GEORGE R.

TRUSTY and Well-beloved, We greet you well: Whereas We are graciously pleased, fur divers good cause*

and considerations Us hereunto moving, to grant and allow unto Our Right trusty and well-beloved Councillor Henry Lord Viscount Melville, Keeper of Our Privy Seal of Scotland, one Annuity or yearly Sum of One thousand Five hundred Pounds over and above the yearly Fe^ or Salary of Three thousand Pounds, made payable to him by virtue of Our Letters of Privy Seal of date the 10th day of July 1800, referring to the Letters Patent, by which he is constituted Keeper of the said Seal: And Our pleasure is, that the said Annuity or yearly Sum of One thousand

Five hundred Pounds so granted and allowed by Us as aforesaid, shall commence and be accounted payable to the said Henry Lord Melville from the 5th day of July instant, and shall be paid to the said Henry Lonl Viscount Melville, or to his Assigns, during his continuance in the said Office of Keeper of Our said Privy Seal, Quarterly, at the four most usual days of payment in the year, by even and equal portions; but Our Royal intention is, that the said Additional Salary should be payable only as long as the said Viscount Melville shall continue to hold the Office of Keeper of Our Privy Seal in Scotland, and not to be continued to his Successor in that Office: Our will and pleasure is, and We do hereby direct, authorize, and command you to issue your Warrants to the Receiver General of Our Landrenta and Casualties, authorizing and requiring him to pay unto the said Henry Viscount Melville, or to his Assigns, the said sum of One thousand Five hundred Pounds a year, to commence from the 5th day of July 1804, and to be payable and paid to him, or his Assigns, during his continuance in the said Office of Keeper of Our said Privy Seal, Quarterly, at the four most usual days of payment in the year accordingly; but Our Further will and pleasure is, that the said Additional Salary of One thousand Five hundred Pounds a year shall be payable only as long as the said Henry Viscount Melville shall continue to hold the Office of Keeper of Our Privy Seal of Scotland, and not to be continued to his Successors in that Office; And We do hereby charge and command you to cause the said Additional Annuity or yearly Sum of One thousand Five hundred Pounds, and all Payments thereupon, as they shall from time to time become due and payable, to be inserted on the Quarterly Establishments or Lids of Payments of Our Civil Affairs there, so as the sums to be inserted therein may be allowed and paid from time to time in like manner as other the Salaries or Allowances on the fame Lifts shall from time to time be paid; And for so doing this shall be not only to you but to all others herein concerned, a sufficient Warrant, Given at Our Court at Saint James's, the 31ft day of July 1804, in the forty-fourth year of Our Reigo.

Our Chief Raron, and the rest} of Our Barons of Our Court > of Exchequer in Scotland. }

By His Majesty’s Command,

Signed

W. Pitt. C. Long. Lquumc.

King's Warrant; granting Additional ' £,200 per annum to the Royal Academy, for teaching Excrciles at Edinburgh,

GEORGE R. ....

TRUSTY and Well-beloved, We greet you well: Whereas We did, by a Warrant under Our Royal Sign

Manual, bearing date the 17th day of July 1766, direct, authorize, and require you to allow the sum of Two hundred Pounds per annum to the Royal Academy, for teaching Exercises at Edinburgh: And whereas the Commissioners of

Our Treasury have represented unto Us, that it hath been made appear unto them by your Report of the 7th August lad, that the Exercises taught in the said Academy have been attended with great benefit to Scotland, and that the yearly Sum of £. 200, hitherto granted for its support, has not been sufficient for defraying the necessary expeaces thereof, and have therefore recommended unto Us to grant an Addition of Two hundred Pounds per annum to the original sum, to enable the Diredprs and Governors to carry on the Institution under their patronage in a proper manner for the future, to which We being graciously pleased to consent, Our will and pleasure is, and We do hereby direct, authorize, and command you to issue your Warrant or Warrants upon the Receiver General of Our Landrents and Casualties, authorizing and requiring him to pay the Additional Sum of Two hundred Pounds per annum to any person or persons empowered by the Directors and Managers of Our said Academy (or any five of them) to receive the same out of any Our Revenues in that part of Great Britain called Scotland, at Our Royal disposal, and to insert the fame on Our Civil Establishments, to be paid Quarterly, at the four most usual feasts or days of payment in the year, by even and equal portions; the first day's payment to commence from the 10th day of October next to the next quarterly day of payment, and from thenceforth Quarterly, and to continue till the fame be recalled by Us or Our Royal Successors; which said Additional Sum of Two hundred Pounds per annum is to be applied by the said Directors and Managers for encouraging and supporting Our said Academy, and defraying the necessary Expencts thereof: And for so doing this shall be your Warrant. Given at Our Court at Saint James’s, this otli day of

October 1804, in the foity-fourth year of Our Reign.

The Chief Baron, and the rest} of the Barons of Our Court > of Exchequer in Scotland. )

By His Majesty's Command,

Signed

C. Long.
